options.text: Thresh the stalks to detach the grains, then separate husk from the loose grains.
Call the beating of the stalks winnowing, because air will also blow during the work.
Skip threshing, because grains still on stalks can go straight into husk separation.
Blow hard over the unthreshed stalks so the grains fall off by themselves.

stem:
Dhruv's uncle brings harvested wheat stalks. The grains are still stuck to the stalks.

What should they do first before they try to separate grains from husk?

teacher.key_rationale: Threshing detaches grains from stalks first. Only then can husk be separated from the loose grains. Skipping threshing or renaming it winnowing misses that step.
